sector_model: infrastructure engineering software (US filer): P/E GAAP, EV/sales, FCF yield before and after SBC, net debt including convertibles, ARR and net revenue retention
thesis: Bentley Systems (Nasdaq: BSY) sells subscription engineering software for infrastructure. Q3 2026 revenue 421.5M (+12.2%), subscriptions +12.4%, GAAP operating income 122.6M (vs 84.5M), GAAP NI 89.9M, ARR 1,582.8M (+13% constant currency), net revenue retention 110%; Q3 OCF 109.4M (down from 116.4M). TTM revenue 1,648.0M, GAAP NI 322.6M, OCF 516.0M, company-defined FCF 489.3M, SBC about 82M. Debt 1,162.2M (term loan 550M and revolver 40.3M due Oct 2029; 575M convertible notes due July 2027) vs cash 150.9M, net debt about 1,011M (company: 1.7x). At 44.19 (2026-11-12 close; 52-week range 28.08-48.17): market cap about 13.37B on 302.44M shares (Class A 11.52M + Class B 290.92M at 2026-10-29), EV about 14.4B, 8.7x TTM sales, 41x TTM GAAP earnings, FCF yield 3.7% (3.0% after SBC). Quality compounder but not cheap; price is near the top of its range.
counterthesis: The multiple already prices steady low-teens growth: 41x GAAP earnings and a 3% FCF yield after SBC leave little margin for error. FCF fell y/y in 9M (353.1M vs 384.0M) while capex rose; the 2026 notes were refinanced with a floating-rate term loan (SOFR plus 1-2%), and the 575M July 2027 convertible must be settled or refinanced, with 1.7x net leverage. Net share count is falling via buybacks (4.06M Class B for 135.1M in 9M) but convertible dilution is not in the count. AI-driven competition for engineering workflows and infrastructure budget cuts are risks; the Cohesive divestiture (closed 2026-10-13) makes comparisons less clean. A 12% gain from the 52-week low is not a thesis. Peers (Autodesk, PTC, Trimble, Nemetschek), conversion terms and MD&A unread.
invalidation: Thesis weakens if ARR growth falls below 10% constant currency, net retention drops below 105%, or FCF conversion keeps declining. Valuation case needs a price decline to roughly 5%+ FCF yield after SBC, or evidence that growth can sustainably exceed 15%.
